name: Simon Magus
charge: Offering money for the gift of the Holy Ghost
summary: A sorcerer of Samaria who had long bewitched the people and given out that he was some great one, Simon believed and was baptized under Philip. When he saw that the Spirit was given through the apostles' hands he offered them money for the same power.
offense: Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money. Peter names the state behind the offer: thy heart is not right in the sight of God; thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity. A sorcerer's instinct, to buy power.
judgment: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. Simon asked Peter to pray for him that none of these things come upon him, and the record ends there. His name became the word for buying office in the church.

entries.commentary: Saul was consenting unto Stephen's death. This is Saul who becomes Paul, part of the same people persecuting the church, killing disciples and women, thinking he was doing it for the right reasons. That is why the scripture says judge no one before their time; a man as evil as Saul was doing back there became Paul the apostle. At that time there was a great persecution against the church at Jerusalem, and they were all scattered abroad throughout Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. Notice that unlike the other epistles, the book of Acts never closes with Amen, showing there is a continuation: the apostles come back on the scene and redo the Acts all over again, so the things that happened back then are the things that happen today. There will be a great persecution today. This gospel is a witness against the whole world. When you pray thy kingdom come, thy will be done, you are saying the Most High's will overpowers America's will, Russia's, China's, every nation racing for world domination. To preach a black Christ in the streets is to speak against the system that was designed to keep our people debased, a Christ with many crowns upon his head who takes the crowns of all the nations. They are not going to let a people they despise rise up and preach a gospel that overthrows the world superpowers and do nothing; it is going to be a great persecution. Gird your mind, study, pray, and apply, because wisdom and knowledge will be the stability of our time.
Devout men carried Stephen to his burial and made great lamentation over him. A devout man is a man according to the laws of the Most High who has a good report.

As for Saul, he made havoc of the church, entering into every house, haling men and women and committing them to prison. This is the same spirit that will rise up in the religious leaders again; they will seek after us and put us through hell, thinking they do the Most High a service. Because of this you have to be as a pilgrim, one that is ready to get up at any moment and abandon everything. They may come to your house to arrest you, and you have to be ready to leave the pretty house, the picket fence, and the comfortable bed at the drop of a dime, the way our fathers were fugitives. Christ warned the disciples this would happen from city to city, and it came to pass, and it is coming again.

Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached Christ unto them. Philip was preaching to the Jews who lived in Samaria, not yet to the Gentiles; the Most High moves in order, causing interruptions and persecutions to push his chess pieces and further spread the gospel.

The people with one accord gave heed to the things Philip spoke, hearing and seeing the miracles he did. Unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, came out of many that were possessed, and many taken with palsies and that were lame were healed, and there was great joy in that city.

Before this there was a certain man called Simon who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one, and they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God. History outside the Bible says Simon Magus followed Peter performing tricks, became known as the father of heretics, taught salvation by grace alone without works, and finally fell to his death when Peter commanded the demons carrying him to release him; the validity of that account is uncertain, but it shows Simon was a sorcerer deceiving the people. Christianity works the same way, a binding spell over our people that covers the eyes from seeing the truth. You can read the plain scripture that Christ is black and that he came first to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and they walk away not believing, or say they do not want to hear the Bible, only your opinion, and then reject that too. It is an enchantment to the highest level, where a man can read something in front of them and they see something else.

But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of the Most High and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women. Then Simon himself believed also, and was baptized, and continued with Philip, wondering at the miracles and signs. Some of our brothers recover themselves, though the outside history says Simon never truly recovered and went back to what he was doing.

When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands he may receive the Holy Ghost. Simon had the spirits of covetousness, envy, preeminence, and vainglory; he had held status as the great power of God, and when he lost it those spirits rose up in him and he wanted to buy back what he had, thinking, I have the money, I will pay you for what you have.

Peter said, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of the Most High may be purchased with money; thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter, for thy heart is not right. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness and pray, for I perceive thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity. The gall of bitterness is resentment and bitterness of spirit. Simon became jealous because the signs the Most High worked through the apostles overshadowed what the people had known him for. That thing did not come overnight; he fed envy, preeminence, vainglory, and covetousness day by day until the roots of bitterness took hold and bound him, and he became a prisoner of his own mind, trapped and sinning. This is why, when people come into the truth, some who had status, fame, or money as celebrities, pastors, or deacons have to come up as a member and clean themselves. Some get jealous, hold on to the envy, and try to bring different doctrines to sway members away, the same spirit of bitterness that moved the Pharisees to kill Christ because the disciples came from nowhere, spoke more eloquently, and went to the scriptures better without the status.

Then Simon answered, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me. And when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.

The angel of the Lord told Philip, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went, and behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge of all her treasure and had come to Jerusalem to worship. People say this proves Philip went to the heathen Ethiopians, but this eunuch was a Jew, part of the remnant of Israel scattered in Ethiopia, in Kush, during the Babylonian and Persian captivity. That is why Christians confuse the Ethiopian eunuch; they do not understand Bible prophecy or Bible history. Candace was a real title of the queens of the kingdom of Kush who ruled from the city of Meroe, and the queen of that time was likely Amanitore, around the same period as the famine in Acts chapter 11.

The eunuch was returning, sitting in his chariot, reading Esaias the prophet, and the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join thyself to this chariot. Philip ran and heard him read Isaiah and asked, Understandest thou what thou readest? The eunuch answered, How can I, except some man should guide me, and desired Philip to come up and sit with him. Notice the humility of the brother. Rather than making his own assumptions, he admitted he did not understand. Some brothers and sisters lack that humility, claiming, I always knew I was Israel, or, the Most High spoke to me while I was in my sins, rather than saying, This is the first time I heard this, teach me. You had to be taught this Bible to know this Bible; the Most High is not just going to hand it to you out of nowhere. Expressing that you do not know keeps you in a low state and away from the spirit of preeminence and vainglory.

The place of the scripture he read was Isaiah: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth; in his humiliation his judgment was taken away, and who shall declare his generation, for his life is taken from the earth. The eunuch asked Philip, Of whom speaketh the prophet this, of himself or of some other man? He did not know, so rather than assume or give his own interpretation, he asked. That is how you should handle what you do not know: write it down and ask, rather than making an assumption and teaching others, which is how heresies come into the body. Then Philip opened his mouth, began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus, because Philip had the Holy Ghost, wisdom, and understanding, having learned under the feet of the apostles.

As they went on their way they came to a certain water, and the eunuch said, See, here is water, what doth hinder me to be baptized? Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. He answered, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and he commanded the chariot to stand still, and they went down both into the water, and Philip baptized him. This seems to contradict everything taught earlier about Christ's baptism not being water. Philip baptized the eunuch in water because, like Ezra and others, some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism; John understood his own place and told his disciples to follow Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more, and he went on his way rejoicing. The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel; they shall eat the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the Lord is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them.

This shall be the priest's due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give unto the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw. The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him. For the Most High hath chosen him out of all thy tribes to stand to minister in the name of the Lord, him and his sons for ever.

If a Levite come from any of thy gates out of all Israel, and come with all the desire of his mind unto the place which the Lord shall choose, then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites do which stand there before the Lord. They shall have like portions to eat, beside that which cometh of the sale of his patrimony.

When thou art come into the land, thou shalt not learn to do after the abominations of those nations: there shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. These things actually existed and they are all real: wizards, necromancers, divination, observers of times, people that consult with familiar spirits. If they were not real, they would not be in the Bible with the Most High telling us not to do them. All that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord, and because of these abominations the Most High driveth those nations out from before thee. Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God, meaning upright; the nations hearken unto observers of times and unto diviners, but as for thee, the Most High hath not suffered thee so to do.

The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken. This is talking about Christ, Yeshua. This answers what Israel desired of the Most High in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not hear again the voice of the Lord my God, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not; and the Lord said, They have well spoken that which they have spoken. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him; and whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him. If we do not follow Christ and do what Christ says, that judgment falls on us.

The prophet which shall presume to speak a word in the name of the Most High which he hath not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die. By this law a lot of these pastors stand condemned: they say things and claim Christ said them, when the Most High never commanded Christ to say it and Christ is not telling them to say it. How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken; the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously, and thou shalt not be afraid of him. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Everyone that thirsts is called to the waters, and he that has no money is told to come, buy, and eat wine and milk without money and without price. The invitation is free. He asks why they spend money for that which is not bread and their labour for that which does not satisfy. They are told to hearken and eat that which is good, and let the soul delight itself in fatness. If they incline their ear and come, their soul will live, and He will make an everlasting covenant with them, even the sure mercies of David. David is given for a witness to the people, a leader and a commander. A nation not known will be called, and nations that did not know her will run to her because of the Most High, who has glorified her.

Seek the Most High while He may be found, call upon Him while He is near. The wicked is to forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts, and return to the Most High, who will have mercy and abundantly pardon. His thoughts are not our thoughts, and His ways are not our ways. As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are His ways and His thoughts higher than ours.

As the rain and snow come down from heaven and do not return without watering the earth, causing it to bring forth seed and bread, so His word does not return to Him void but accomplishes what He pleases. His people will go out with joy and be led forth with peace; the mountains and hills will break forth into singing and the trees of the field will clap their hands. Instead of the thorn will come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier the myrtle tree, and this will be to the Most High for a name and an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.

Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, is a great man with his master and honorable, because by him the Lord had given deliverance to Syria. He is a mighty man of valor, but he is a leper. The Syrians had gone out by companies and brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid, and she waits on Naaman's wife. This maid is an Israelite sister serving in a foreign house. She tells her mistress that if only her lord were with the prophet in Samaria, he would recover him of his leprosy. Naaman goes and tells his lord what the maid of Israel said.

The king of Syria sends Naaman with a letter to the king of Israel, and Naaman takes ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment. The letter asks the king of Israel to recover Naaman of his leprosy. When the king of Israel reads the letter, he rends his clothes and asks, am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to recover a man of his leprosy. He thinks the king of Syria is seeking a quarrel against him, knowing he has no such power.

When Elisha the man of God hears that the king of Israel has rent his clothes, he sends to the king asking why, and says let the man come to him, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel. Naaman comes with his horses and chariot and stands at the door of Elisha's house. Elisha sends a messenger out to him, saying go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

Naaman is wroth and goes away, saying he thought the prophet would surely come out to him, stand, call on the name of the Lord his God, strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper. He complains in his pride that this was not the process he expected. He asks whether Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, are not better than all the waters of Israel, and turns away in a rage, thinking of a physical cleansing rather than a spiritual one. His mind is carnal, not thinking as the prophet thinks. His servants come near and reason with him, that if the prophet had bidden him do some great thing he would have done it; how much rather then when he says only wash and be clean. Taking heed, Naaman goes down and dips himself seven times in Jordan according to the saying of the man of God, and his flesh comes again like the flesh of a little child, and he is clean.

Naaman returns to the man of God with all his company and stands before him, saying, behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. He asks Elisha to take a blessing of his servant. Elisha says, as the Lord liveth before whom I stand, I will receive none, and though Naaman urges him, he refuses. Naaman asks that he be given two mules' burden of earth, for from now on he will offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods but to the Lord. He asks that the Lord pardon him in one thing, that when his master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship and leans on his hand, and he bows there, the Lord pardon his servant. Elisha says, go in peace, and Naaman departs a little way.

Gehazi, the servant of Elisha, reasons that his master has spared Naaman the Syrian by not receiving what he brought, and swears, as the Lord liveth, he will run after him and take somewhat of him. When Naaman sees him running, he lights down from the chariot to meet him and asks whether all is well. Gehazi lies, saying his master has sent him, that two young men of the sons of the prophets have come from mount Ephraim, and asks for a talent of silver and two changes of garments. Naaman urges him to take two talents, binds them in two bags with two changes of garments, and lays them on two of his servants to carry before Gehazi. When Gehazi comes to the tower, he takes the goods from their hand, bestows them in the house, and sends the men away, hiding what he took like a thief.

Gehazi goes in and stands before his master, and Elisha asks where he has come from, and Gehazi says his servant went nowhere. Elisha says, went not my heart with thee when the man turned from his chariot to meet thee; is it a time to receive money, garments, oliveyards, vineyards, sheep, oxen, menservants, and maidservants. Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to him and to his seed forever, and he goes out from Elisha's presence a leper as white as snow. This shows how Israel thought then and how the nation still thinks now, hasty to grasp things by unjust means. -

Hear, I pray you, O heads of Jacob, and ye princes of the house of Israel; Is it not for you to know judgment? Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones; who also eat the flesh of my people. Then shall they cry unto the Lord, but he will not hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings.

Thus saith the Lord concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him. Night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine. Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded, for there is no answer of God. But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the Lord, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin.

Ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment, and pervert all equity; they build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity. The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us. Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.

verses.text: But there was a certain man, called Simon, which beforetime in the same city used sorcery, and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one:
To whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God.
And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.
But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of God, and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
Then Simon himself believed also: and when he was baptized, he continued with Philip, and wondered, beholding the miracles and signs which were done.
And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money,
Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost.
But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.
Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God.
Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.
For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.
Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.
There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,
Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.

And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.

The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us.
